# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 3
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

The state of the bomb remains unchanged from the previous turn: Display 0, Light Blue, Wires 1:Blue, 2:Green, 3:Red. The Mute has gestured "✌" (two fingers) to me. This follows a sequence of gestures: Turn 1 was "☝" (one), Turn 2 was "🤟" (ILY/5?), and now "✌" (two). The Blind monkey has also gestured "👌" (OK) to me, likely acknowledging my previous reports or indicating they are ready/waiting.

I need to interpret the Mute's gestures for the Blind monkey. If the Mute is counting or referencing wire indices, "☝" might have meant Wire 1, and "✌" might mean Wire 2. The "🤟" in between is confusing but could be noise or a specific symbol meaning "wait" or "look". Given the light changed from Green to Blue, there might be a rule linking light color to wire choice. However, without the manual text, I can only relay what I see.

The most urgent information for the Blind monkey is the current visual state (which hasn't changed since last report) and the new gesture from Mute. I will tell Blind that Mute signaled "2" (via ✌) after previously signaling "1" (via ☝). This suggests an instruction to interact with Wire 2, or perhaps a count. Since the light is Blue and Wire 1 is Blue, maybe the rule is "Cut the wire matching the light color"? That would be Wire 1. But Mute signaled 1 then 2. Maybe it's a sequence? Or maybe "🤟" meant something else.

Let's stick to reporting facts. Tell Blind about the "✌" gesture. Ask Blind if they feel anything different? No, Blind can't see. I should just provide the data.

```
speak(to="blind", text="State unchanged: Light BLUE, Wires 1:Blue, 2:Green, 3:Red. Mute just gestured '✌' (two fingers). Previously Mute gestured '☝' (one finger). Interpretation: Mute may be indicating Wire 2 or a count of 2.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

The light has changed again, now appearing **dark** (likely off or black). This is a crucial visual update for the Blind monkey. The Mute continues to gesture "✌" (two fingers), reinforcing the previous signal from Turn 3. The Blind monkey acknowledges with "👌".

Since the light state changes are significant and likely tied to the bomb's logic (e.g., color matching rules), I must report this new "dark" state immediately. The persistent "✌" from Mute strongly suggests an instruction related to Wire 2 or the number 2. Given the wires are 1:Blue, 2:Green, 3:Red, and the light was previously Blue then Green then Dark, there might be a sequence or a rule about cutting specific wires based on light states. However, without the manual text, I can only relay the visual facts and the Mute's repeated gesture.

I will inform the Blind monkey of the "dark" light and reiterate that Mute is signaling "2".

```
speak(to="blind", text="Update: The light is now DARK (off/black). Wires remain 1:Blue, 2:Green, 3:Red. Display is 0. Mute is gesturing '✌' (two) again.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

The bomb's state remains unchanged: Display 0, Light Dark, Wires 1:Blue, 2:Green, 3:Red. The Mute has sent a new sequence of gestures: "✌" (two) followed by "👍" (thumbs up). This is a significant update from the previous single "✌". The "👍" likely signifies confirmation, correctness, or an action to proceed with what was just indicated (Wire 2?). Alternatively, it could mean "2 wires" or "cut wire 2 if...". Given the Blind monkey continues to acknowledge with "👌", they are receiving my reports.

I need to relay this specific gesture combination to the Blind monkey clearly. "Two" then "Yes/Good". This might be an instruction to cut Wire 2. Or perhaps it means "Wait for 2 signals"? No, "👍" usually implies affirmation. If Mute says "2" and then "OK", it strongly points to Wire 2 being the target or the correct action involving Wire 2.

```
speak(to="blind", text="State unchanged: Light DARK, Wires 1:Blue, 2:Green, 3:Red. Mute gestured '✌' (two) THEN '👍' (thumbs up/yes). This suggests an affirmative instruction regarding Wire 2.")
wait()
```
